picks.file: A Triumphal Arch at Laodicea - Pococke Richard - 1745.jpg
picks.what: The Roman four-way arch (tetrapylon), engraving in Richard Pococke, A Description of the East
picks.why: the city’s best-known ancient monument, still standing; ground plan below trimmed off

picks.what: The harbor and its sea castle, colored aquatint in Luigi Mayer, Views in the Ottoman Dominions
picks.why: color general view of the port with the castle, town walls, minaret and ships; caption and plate margins trimmed off

picks.file: View of the Temple of Bacchus, Laodicea-Lattakia - Texier Charles - 1864.jpg
picks.what: The Roman colonnade known as the Temple of Bacchus, lithograph in Charles Texier, Byzantine Architecture
picks.why: landmark scene: the Roman columns with the domed building behind; only usable view for 1850–1913

gaps: P0–P1: nothing usable (an Apocalypse miniature of Laodicea in Asia Minor); P5: kept the existing 1921 autochrome; P6: nothing (lake views elsewhere in the province, a space photo, fishing boats)
notes: The 1866 photo (#9) was skipped: 1866 is the founding year of the Beirut studio printed on the mount, not the date of the picture. Borra’s 1750 “Valley of Laodicea” (#5) shows Laodicea on the Lycus in Turkey. The other 1921 Gadmer views (#11, #12) are not clearly better than the existing one. Pococke’s plates for Syria are in vol. 2, published 1745 (Commons gives 1743).
